details: Radiant flux follows Stefan-Boltzmann: q = sigma T^4. At 1200 C (1473 K) that is about 267 kW/m2.
A flash fire is about 84 kW/m2; lava surface flux is roughly three times that, before convection and conduction.
Aluminized surfaces reflect most radiant load, but conducted heat through boots and ground contact still kills time fast.
Human survival time collapses as flux rises: protection is measured in seconds even with the best reflective gear.
